newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures mostly lower, bullion rises.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures mostly lower, bullion rises.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended mostly lower, pressured by the yen's gains against the dollar, while gold bullion extended early gains as bullish sentiment carried over from New York trade, traders said.
Activity was relatively buoyant. Most-active benchmark April gold ended 10 yen per gram lower at 1,360 yen. Other contract prices ranged from 13 yen lower to six yen up.
At 0724 GMT, spot gold was quoted firmer at $344.35/85 per ounce, against $343.50/344.00 in New York on Thursday.
"A sharp slide in the dollar provided impetus to help push gold out of its recent $340-343 range," one trader said.
Private investors built fresh longs in distant months from the outset, believing gold futures prices were relatively low, while trade houses bought spot gold in arbitrage dealings.
The trader said further gains in spot gold could be limited unless fresh incentives emerge.
Platinum futures were marginally weaker while palladium futures settled mixed.

Despite expectations that Russian exports of PGM will resume soon, supply tightness in the spot market helped limit losses in yen-based futures and caused spot platinum and palladium prices to rise during Asian hours, traders said.
A spokesman for the U.S. branch of Russia's platinum group metal export agency, Almaz said on Thursday that a decree authorising export quotas for PGMs had been signed on Monday.
"High lease rates caused by tightness in the spot market, made traders wary of building short positions," a trader said.
Platinum short-term lease rates were around 8-10 percent, traders said. Benchmark April platinum closed seven weaker at 1,457 yen.
Benchmark April palladium ended down five at 591 yen while benchmark April silver finished 0.3 yen per 10 grams up at 193.0 yen. --Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
